targets.outcome_robustness_quote:
The second column in Table 4 is the same analysis, but using the COVID19 compliance items from the COUNSELING24 November endline, gathered three
months after the INFO24 August endline.11 In this data, the COUNSELING24
treatment has a large eﬀect on compliance, raising scores by 1.357 SD (p<0.001),
while the INFO24 treatment eﬀects have largely disappeared. The eﬀect of receiving a INFO24 call (but no COUNSELING24 treatment) has fallen from 1.781 SD
(p<0.001) to 0.254 SD (p<0.05), while the initially stronger “Call+SMS” eﬀect has
been erased – going from 2.808 SD (p<0.001) to 0.086 (p=0.421).
targets.outcome_reasoning: The report says it reproduces and assesses the original package but does not explicitly establish numerical agreement with the original published outputs. Its statement that coauthors reproduced all their analyses concerns this report’s own analyses, so it cannot settle original computational reproducibility. Linked alternative compliance outcomes for the same respondents greatly reduce or remove INFO24 effects; the data audit also substantively challenges design validity. Confidence is low for computation and high for the robustness challenge.
